releases.name: AnyPS5 Studio v1.5.1
releases.body:
AnyPS5 Studio 1.5.1 updates the bundled AnyPS5 core from v0.1.2 to **[v0.1.4](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/releases/tag/v0.1.4)**.

## Changes
- **AnyPS5 core v0.1.4**: the bundled relinker and system libraries now come from the latest upstream release. Existing installs switch to it automatically the next time Studio starts, and each game receives the new libraries on its next launch.
- **Relink hint**: Studio now remembers which core relinked each game. If a game was relinked with an earlier core, the launch log says so and suggests relinking it in Relinker Studio if it fails to start.
- **Verified core downloads**: the bundled core is checked against the SHA-256 checksums AnyPS5 publishes for the release; a mismatch stops the build.
- The NID inspector's "Python 3 not found" message now points to the correct re-audit button.

## After updating
If a game that worked before no longer starts, open **Relinker Studio** and relink it.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ramsforge/AnyPS5-Studio/compare/v1.5.0...v1.5.1

releases.name: AnyPS5 Studio v1.5.0
releases.body:
AnyPS5 Studio 1.5.0 is the biggest update so far: full controller support, playtime tracking, safer handling of your game folders, a faster app that works offline, and a round of security hardening.

## Highlights

### Full controller navigation
- Use the D-pad / left stick to move around every screen (menus, Settings, dialogs, setup and the launcher). Cross selects, Circle goes back, L1 / R1 switch tabs.
- On the game row, Left / Right still pick a game and Cross plays it; press Down to reach the game's buttons.
- Studio ignores the controller while you are playing a game, so button presses never reach Studio behind it.
- Controller rumble now follows the Haptic Feedback setting.
- Arrow keys and Escape work the same way on the keyboard.

### Playtime tracking
- Total playtime and your last session are recorded for every game and shown on the home screen.

### Safer game folders
- Studio only reorganizes folders that actually contain a PS5 title, and no longer moves game assets just because their name looks like a backup (for example `*.baked`).

releases.body:
# X360 Mobile 0.6.6

- Integrated Xenia Edge upstream through November 20, 2026. This brings updates across CPU and system emulation, graphics, audio and game content handling while preserving X360 Mobile's Android features and existing fixes.
- Improved handling of game updates and Android storage access. Updated the in-game interface and input handling.
- Continued work on reducing shader-related pauses at the beginning of **Fable II**. New scenes can still pause while shaders are prepared.

Focused checks on Odin 2 covered gameplay in **GTA IV**, **Forza Horizon 2** and **Fable II**, as well as pause, resume and shutdown in **Assassin's Creed**. Results can vary across titles, devices and drivers.

TV mode, synced player profiles and picture-in-picture remain experimental. You can install this release over your current version.

releases.name: X360 Mobile 0.6.5 Hotfix 8
releases.body:
# X360 Mobile 0.6.5 Hotfix 8

This update improves graphics accuracy and adds better diagnostic information for investigating driver performance reports.

## General graphics correction

- Corrected a graphics accuracy issue observed as temporary black, blue or multicoloured corruption during the opening of **Fable II**.
- The correction applies automatically and may also help other games affected by similar rendering problems. No additional game setting is required for this correction; existing recommended settings remain available.
- Verified through two opening runs reaching the first childhood gameplay scene on Odin 2. Later scenes, full campaigns and other GPUs still need testing.
- This is an accuracy improvement, with no general FPS increase promised. Brief pauses may still occur when new shaders are prepared.

## Driver diagnostics and session sharing

- Added more useful texture and performance information for investigating reported slowdowns with **RADV on Exynos/Xclipse**.
- Gameplay measurement recordings are now associated with their session and can be included when using **Share session bundle** from Session history.

releases.name: X360 Mobile 0.6.5 Hotfix 7
releases.body:
# X360 Mobile 0.6.5 Hotfix 7

This update brings a general graphics correctness improvement and experimental picture-in-picture support for external media apps.

## Graphics correction

- Fixed the horizontally divided image and missing lower portion observed in the opening real-time cutscene of **Kingdoms of Amalur: Reckoning**.
- This is a general core correction, applied automatically without additional settings. It may benefit other games affected by similar rendering problems, but wider game and GPU coverage still needs testing.
- Verified through repeated starts and progression to character creation on Odin 2. This does not certify the full campaign or promise a general FPS increase.

## Experimental picture-in-picture

- Keep the game full screen while a compatible external media app uses Android's floating video window.
- Added an app selector with PiP compatibility indicators, an optional media link, and controls in the game menu. Find these options under **Settings → App → Appearance and startup**.

releases.name: X360 Mobile 0.6.5 Hotfix 6
releases.body:
# X360 Mobile 0.6.5 Hotfix 6

Maintenance update focused on optional driver compatibility and updated game recommendations.

- Added an optional experimental texture compatibility setting for RADV on Samsung Xclipse. It is disabled by default and has not yet been verified on Xclipse hardware. Successful driver loading, rendering and performance are not guaranteed; memory use may increase.
- Added recommended settings for **Mobile Suit Gundam: Operation Troy**, restoring the visible world in the first map tested on Odin 2. A complete game copy is required; other devices and the full campaign remain unverified.
- Added recommendations for **Sonic Free Riders with the adapted No Kinect mod**. The compatible adapted mod and its designated launcher are required: settings alone do not repair the original mod, and the mod is not bundled with the app. Menus and two tutorial stages were tested; uneven steering remains under investigation, and full-game compatibility is not confirmed.

releases.name: X360 Mobile 0.6.5 Hotfix 5
releases.body:
# X360 Mobile 0.6.5 Hotfix 5

Maintenance update focused on game loading reliability and clearer driver diagnostics.

- Improved handling of extracted games, disc images and installed game containers.
- Added a per-game startup executable selector for games with multiple launchers.
- Improved reliability when loading additional game modules and title updates, with safer recovery after failed launches.
- Improved recognition of game files and preservation of launch preferences across library updates and shortcuts.
- More precise on-device Vulkan driver diagnostics, including the image check that failed and available error information.

Custom drivers remain device-dependent. More detailed diagnostics help investigate compatibility; they do not guarantee successful RADV loading or fix every game or mod.

Install over your current version; no uninstall is required. Keep a backup of your profiles and saves as usual.

# FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE · Android 原生移植版 v1.1.0 发布说明

- **版本号**：`v1.1.0`（`versionCode=80`，`org.ffrs.gamewindow`）
- **通用安装包**：`FFRS-1.1.0-universal.apk`（`arm64-v8a`，全平台通用）

---

## 本版本主要更新

### 1. 通用性能优化（骁龙 / 天玑全平台适用）
- **描述符与同步热路径优化**：新增图形 `PushMemo` 负载缓存、`PushMemoTexel` 原地刷新与 `SlotSets` 惰性分配，大幅降低重复描述符构建开销；扩大 `push_memo_map` 容量上限至 `32768`，避免复杂大场景频繁整表清空。
- **瞬态着色器自适应旁路**：新增 `PushMemoShaderState` 机制，自动识别连续未命中的瞬态着色器并临时旁路查表，减少无效哈希计算。
- **屏障与状态查询精简**：收窄 `texel` 与 `compute_barrier()` 管线屏障，合并 `pending_view()` 单趟重叠检查，缓存 `VkFormatProperties3` 并跳过只读纹理的重复 `prepare_read`。
- **洞窟场景闪烁修复**：修复洞窟路段左右移动时偶发的右半屏隔帧闪烁问题，保持全场景画面完整稳定输出。

### 2. 完整内置功能
- **画质与帧率设置**（顶部菜单 `≡` → **画质与帧率**）：
  - **帧率上限**：支持 `沿用原设置 / 30 FPS / 40 FPS / 60 FPS`，调节后实时生效，无需重启。
  - **画面输出档位**：支持 `沿用原设置 / 720p 输出 / 1080p 输出`，保存并重开游戏后生效。
- **内置中文金手指**（顶部菜单 `≡` → **金手指**，勾选保存并重启生效）：
  - 移动速度 2 倍
  - 不遇敌（按住 R3 临时恢复正常）
  - 战斗掉落率 100%
  - 战斗经验值 2 倍
  - 战斗金币 2 倍
  - 角色存档修改

### 3. 虚拟手柄默认布局优化
- 缩小肩键（`L1/L2/R1/R2`）与功能键（`- / +`）尺寸，将肩键下移至左右中侧边缘，避免遮挡左上角帧率/任务信息与右上角小地图。
- 对称对齐左右摇杆、`L3/R3`、十字键与 `A/B/X/Y` 菱形按键间距，默认布局更紧凑清晰（仍支持在「编辑按键布局」中自由微调或重置）。

---

## 安装与使用提示
- 请确保设备存储根目录已放置合法导出的游戏数据目录 `/sdcard/FFRS`。

# Let's Go Launcher 0.3

This is the third release of Let's Go Launcher. It brings the game from barely playable on Mali to a real frame rate on weak devices, and fixes the boot failure that stopped the game from opening on some phones.

## Measured performance (Galaxy S20+, Mali-G77, heavy scene)

- **~13.6 fps → 16–20 fps, average ~17.6, peak 20.1** (measured over a 73-second session in the heavy scene; the previous build averaged ~13.6 fps there)
- The game is now GPU-bound (~96% GPU busy, ~23% CPU) — the CPU is no longer the wall
- With a warm pipeline cache, indoor battles reached 23–26 fps
- No crashes in the test session

## What's new in 0.3

- **Boots where it didn't before** — the guest memory base moved from 0x60 to 0x50 (v0132), fixing the launch failure on devices where that range is occupied

Changes since the latest beta release:
- Fixed two UI issues (#843, #846)
- Fixed a bug in the CBM file system implementation (#853)
- Fixed a bug in the drive idle logic (#854)
- Fixed three drive-related VICE tests (#668, #674, #675)

Core and API

* Public API: The API now has as new shape. There are async counterparts (…Async) for state-changing calls, set is now setAsync, there is a new MemoryDebugger API, more getters, and suspend/resume coverage across the API.
* Threading: The command queue and message queue are now std::deque-based. Messages can carry exceptions. AudioPort is thread-safe. Cmd::CALL, TRACK_ON and TRACK_OFF are new.
* Messages: Msg::CONFIG is sent for every option change. ROM_LOADED, RSH_DONE and CONFIG_ERROR are new.
* RetroShell: It has the new architecture from vAmiga, with multiple shells and a single console per shell.
* Workspaces: A screenshot is now saved inside saveWorkspace().
* X-Ray: GPU X-Ray support is added, with a new XRAY_COMPOSITOR option.
* Shared libraries: utlib and rvlib were merged with the versions shared with vAmiga and Silicium.
* Cleanup: Header, include and namespace cleanups, plus removal of orphaned files.

Fixes

* Drive::isIdle() is fixed (#854).

This maintenance release primarily addresses issue #851, which prevented the app from running on the upcoming macOS 27 Golden Gate. It also includes internal code changes required to make the core compatible with the architecture of the upcoming Silicium emulator.
Removing beta status, as no significant bugs have been reported for some time.

## Refactoring

This beta release introduces substantial changes to the underlying code base. As part of the development of the RetroVault app, a new **RetroVault** library has been created. This library is now responsible for managing:

- File systems  
- Devices  
- All supported image formats  

RetroVault is designed as a standalone library and is also used in the latest version of vAmiga for the same purpose.

In addition, the new **utlib** library has been introduced. All utility functions previously embedded in vAmiga and VirtualC64 have been refactored into this more powerful shared library. This makes it easier for me to share common functionality among the different emulators. 

## Enhancements

- The disassembler now supports symbol files (#837)

## Bug Fixes

- Fixed a crash in the file system importer when importing excessively large folders (#841)  
- Fixed a bug in the VIC inspector that prevented selecting individual sprites in Tahoe (#840)

releases.name: CapyPS5 v0.1.0 (beta)
releases.body:
CapyPS5 0.1.0 is the **first beta**: faster on every game, fewer crashes, and on-screen controls you can lay out yourself. PS4 backward compatibility stays experimental. Existing installs are offered this update in the app.

**Faster**
- **The GPU thread runs on the fastest CPU cores.** On a Snapdragon 8 Elite this alone made a demanding Unreal Engine 4 level about a third faster.
- **Less waiting for the GPU.** Several cases where the emulator stopped to read back data the GPU had just written are gone:
  - fast-clear metadata fills now run on the CPU;
  - GPU-driven draws of PS4 games are executed on the GPU;
  - fresh buffer data is copied without a system call per page.
  The same level gained about 30 % more on top.
- **Cheaper per-draw work:** shader resource tables are read in one go per table on ARM, which halved the cost of preparing each draw.

**More stable**
- Unreal Engine games that closed with a corrupt memory error a few seconds into a level (the game's own allocator reporting a broken "canary", or a crash reading address 1) no longer do: the emulator stopped waiting for a GPU signal that was only late.

Fifth alpha of the first PlayStation 5 emulator for Android. Mali GPUs on their system driver can now run games, and the FPS counter shows how many frames CapyPS5 Framegen adds. Existing installs are offered this update in the app.

**New**
- **Mali on the system driver:** that driver cannot sample BCn compressed textures, so the GPU used to be rejected. CapyPS5 now decompresses those textures on the GPU when it uploads them (BC1 to BC7, including BC6H HDR textures). GPUs that support BCn keep using it directly.
- **PanVK on Mali:** the GPU is no longer rejected when the driver lacks vertex-stage stores or dual-source blending.
- **Framegen counter:** with CapyPS5 Framegen on, the FPS counter reads *XX FPS - YY FG*: XX are the game's own frames, YY the total including generated ones. The options are now called *Framegen x2*, *x3* and *x4*.

releases.name: Catherine port v0.1.6
releases.body:
## The sushi bar scene, fixed for real, and shadows for the first time (v0.1.5 was a wrong diagnosis)

v0.1.5 did not fix the *Kappa Heaven* scene of the second day. The black shots were gone, but the plates and the conveyor belt that pass right in front of the camera were missing, and a dark line floated across the picture. The explanation in the v0.1.5 notes was wrong. Please update.

What was actually wrong is a bug in how the port translates this game's shaders. Its vertex shaders come in two halves, and when the port joined them it converted depth twice. That had three effects in every version that used the original depth format (v0.1.0, v0.1.1, v0.1.3 and v0.1.4):

- The near clipping plane sat at half its distance, so geometry the console cuts away was drawn. In those sushi bar shots the camera is inside a wall, and the port drew that wall over the whole shot.
- The depth buffer was squeezed into half its range (0.5 to 1), so the depth of field compared its focus settings against wrong depths. This is where the blur problems of earlier versions came from.
- The shadow maps were stored with the same wrong depth, so no cast shadow ever showed.

releases.name: v0.1.2
releases.body:
## Cutscenes and the title screen are sharp (the real fix)

Close-ups in the *Golden Playhouse* cutscenes (the ones with the black bars) could still come out blurred from edge to edge, faces included, and the title screen looked out of focus. v0.1.1 blamed a short block of shader constants; that was wrong: the depth-of-field pass never reads those bytes.

The real cause is the depth format. The game never tells the graphics API which depth range it uses, and the port assumed the OpenGL-style one, which stores depth squeezed into 0.5–1. The game's depth-of-field planes come straight from each cutscene's data and are written for a plain 0–1 depth, so a face in a close-up landed *behind* the focus plane and the whole frame got the maximum blur. When the game does not choose, the port now uses 0–1 depth, so close-ups keep the face sharp and blur only the background, as intended.

- Checked on the Flip 2: the title screen (same shot before/after: background, piano and characters go from blurred to sharp), the host's introduction, the opening credits, the opening nightmare cutscene and the first puzzle stage, at 30 fps.

This version is backwards compatible with save states from SameBoy 0.14.3 and newer, as well as save states from any BESS compliant emulator

## New/Improved Features
* The libretro core now supports API extensions to retrieve additional metadata and create more portable battery save files
* The iOS frontend has been updated with improved iOS 27 support
* iPhone Duo support was added to the iOS frontend
* The CRT scaling filter has been updated with an improved look
* A new Pixelated/Sharp Bilinear scaling filter
    * This new filter is now the default filter in the Cocoa and SDL frontends
* VFS support was added to the libretro core
* Logging support was added to the libretro core
* The libretro core will now render audio directly in the frontend's audio sample rate, if supported
* Recording audio to a VGM log file is now possible in the Cocoa and SDL frontends
* Minor UI improvements in the Cocoa frontend

## Accuracy Improvements/Fixes
* Workboy emulation now correctly reports the current weekday
* Fixed a bug that made certain small ROM files be incorrectly detected as MMM01 cartridges
* More accurate emulation of SGB command processing

## Bug Fixes

## New/Improved Features
* Added support for more controllers in the iOS frontend, including singular Joy-Cons

* It is now possible to adjust the maximum rumble strength
* It is now possible to modify and save a running ROM file from the Memory Viewer in the Cocoa frontend
* Controller buttons can now be assigned to one of 4 hotkey commands in the iOS frontend
* Periodic saves were added to the iOS frontend
* A new screenshot hotkey was added to the SDL frontend
* Controller UI hiding in the iOS frontend can now optionally disable the centering of the game screen

This version is backwards compatible with save states from SameBoy 0.14.3 and newer, as well as save states from any BESS compliant emulator

## New/Improved Features
* New `usage` debugger command, displaying the Game Boy CPU's time outside of halt/stop modes
* The debugger window in the Cocoa frontend now has a CPU usage graph
* The debugger `print`/`eval` command no longer adds zero padding by default
* The Cocoa frontend now has an option to force an integer scaling factor with black borders, similar to the SDL frontend
* The iOS frontend can now configure rapid A and rapid B buttons on a controller
* The SDL frontend now supports two optional V-sync modes
* The Cocoa and iOS frontends were updated with UI and UX improvements for macOS and iOS 26, respectively
    * This also includes new icons when using on these operating systems, as well as on watchOS 26
* Minor UI improvements were also done for older versions of macOS and iOS
* SameBoy now supports the new menu bar on iPad OS 26
* Improved frame skipping during turbo mode
* Turbo mode can now have a configurable speed cap on all frontends

This version is backwards compatible with save states from SameBoy 0.14.3 and newer, as well as save states from any BESS compliant emulator

## New/Improved Features
* UI improvements to the Cocoa palette editor
* Improved audio quality on libretro; audio is now rendered by SameBoy at 2MHz, and downsampling is now handled by the libretro frontend itself
    * In the Wii U build, downsampling is still done by SameBoy
* With the meaning of register `$FF75` discovered, it is now referred to as `rPGB` in the debugger
* The output of the `watchpoint` debugger command now includes the watchpoint type (read-only, write-only, or read-write)
    * This makes the default watchpoint type (write-only) more obvious
* Windows 11 users can now optionally disable rounded corners in the Graphics Options menu
* Official Windows builds no longer require installing MSVC runtimes by linking against `mvscrt.dll`
* Major improvements to debugging in the SDL frontend:
    * The main emulator window is no longer unresponsive when the debugger is stopped
    * Pressing keys in the emulator window while the debugger is paused now triggers a terminal bell

releases.name: OpenROM v4.1.0
releases.body:
## OpenROM v4.1.0

Universal Retro Gaming Toolkit for retro gaming enthusiasts.

Each download includes:
- **OpenROM** — Flutter desktop GUI
- **openrom-core** — headless CLI (used internally by the GUI)

### CLI usage
```
openrom-core --detect game.iso
openrom-core --input game.iso --format CHD
openrom-core --folder /roms/ --format CHD --compression Max
openrom-core --list-formats
```

### Supported Formats
- PS1/Dreamcast/Saturn/Sega CD: BIN/CUE → CHD (createcd)
- PS2/GameCube/Wii: ISO → CHD (createdvd), CSO, RVZ
- Xbox: ISO → CHD (createdvd), CSO (XISO via community extension)
- PSP: ISO → CSO
- Universal: ZIP/7Z compression, IPS/BPS/xdelta3/DCP patching

Restored entries are checked; a mismatch disables the shortcut for the process. The original path is used after the first network socket opens. Find the switch under **Settings > Additional > Controls**, between Split zones and Order confirmation. This speeds up calculations, not hero animations or AI difficulty.
- Grow the OpenGL ES upload ring when consecutive frames outgrow it, avoiding repeated per-draw allocations in dense adventure views.

releases.name: recomp-launcher 0.3.0
releases.body:
### Added
- The installer shows its version (the game's tag, or the short commit for a
  build off a branch) in the window's corner and title, and on start asks
  GitHub for the game's newest release: a newer one gets a download button.
  Offline it says nothing.
- `game.files` takes globs: `*.iso` makes a folder holding a disc image the
  game, for a title whose setup takes an image rather than an install.
- `installer.yml` takes `platforms` (default `windows linux macos`), so a
  Windows-only game doesn't publish installers that can't build it.
- A `game.files` entry may be alternatives, `a|b`: `HOVER.EXE|hover*.zip` is
  the game's folder or a folder holding a zip of it.

- The Windows installer carries version info and a manifest, and a release
  has `SHA256SUMS.txt`, so antivirus heuristics and players can check it.
- A log of why the installer stopped (`%APPDATA%\recomp-launcher\launcher.log`
  on Windows), and an error box instead of the window vanishing.

### Fixed
- On Windows a step line after a blank line was glued to the line before it
  (ConPTY skips the blank line with a cursor move), so the bar missed that step.

releases.body:
v0.7.7 fixes the Android surface orientation: the v0.7.6 build restored the identity-preferred swapchain preTransform that had shipped in v0.7.5, and on devices reporting ROTATE_90 the composer applied that rotation a second time to an already-upright window-space blit. The game UI rendered sideways and the touch overlay and cursor left the visible area, which is why the on-screen cursor and some options panels (e.g. the Display tab) did not appear where expected.

# Swap2-Native 0.2.0.2-beta

Less memory trouble in heavy places, a clearer "Compiling shaders" screen, and Pokémon Pokopia's shader update made short.

**Install over 0.2.0.1-beta.** Games, packs, mods, saves and shader libraries are kept, and nothing is prepared again.

## Fixed

- **A game that slows to a crawl when the phone runs out of memory** (Zelda: Ocarina of Time entering Castle Town on a 16 GB phone fell to under 1 fps for minutes). The texture cache now notices when the phone starts swapping the game out and stops growing instead. If a game still stutters in big areas, turn on **RAM saving** (Game settings) and close other apps.
- **Zelda: Ocarina of Time on phones with 12 GB of RAM or less** uses less memory for textures and graphics memory (from Banana Native).
- **The "Compiling shaders" screen** shows its whole text on two lines (the time left and "Tap to skip" were cut off), and its bar follows the count.
- **Pokémon Pokopia** updates its shaders quickly after installing 0.2.0: about 60 shaders instead of all of them.

releases.name: Swap2-Native 0.2.0.1-beta
releases.body:
# Swap2-Native 0.2.0.1-beta

A fix for 0.2.0-beta: no more black screen while a game prepares its pipelines.

**Install over 0.2.0-beta.** Games, packs, mods, saves and shader libraries are kept, and nothing is translated or prepared again.

## Fixed

- **A black screen at the first start of a game** (seen with Turnip drivers, for example on a Redmagic 11 Air). Since 0.2.0, a game prepares its known pipelines before it plays (at most 90 seconds). The loading screen had already gone by then, so the game looked stuck. Now the loading screen stays and shows **Compiling shaders: N of M**; tap it to skip the rest. On Turnip the pipelines are made one at a time, so the first start takes the full 90 seconds unless you skip; the next starts are short.

Everything else is as in [0.2.0-beta](https://github.com/mamcjr/Swap2-Native/releases/tag/v0.2.0-beta).

## Thanks

**moceure and the Banana Native contributors**, **enjoyerofslop / DroidPlay Core**, **Sergii "iOrange" Kudlai** (bcdec), **erickmendes22** and **EddizEge / AnkaNative**. Licenses and attribution are included in the sources.

Linux and Windows stay on Alpha 2.2.1: https://github.com/thebabyhippo303/nimbus-recompilation-project/releases/tag/alpha-2.2.1

# Nimbus Alpha 2.2.2 for Android

A second hotfix for Android. Linux and Windows stay on 2.2.1.

## Fixed

- **Phones that still showed "Nimbus could not start graphics" on 2.2.1** (for example some Helio G99 phones on Android 14) now start their games. On these phones Nimbus uses a second graphics path.
- Heads up: the second graphics path is slower than Vulkan, so games on those phones may run slower. Every other device stays on Vulkan.
- Every other device runs exactly as on 2.2.1.

## Good to know

- After updating, Nimbus prepares its shaders once more on the first start.
- Online play is unchanged: 2.2.2 on Android plays with 2.2, 2.2.1 and 2.2.2 on every platform.

## Updating

Install the 2.2.2 APK over 2.2 or 2.2.1. It updates in place and keeps your links and saves. Do not uninstall first.

Thanks to Velkooky on Reddit for finding and reporting this bug.

releases.name: v0.1.0
releases.body:
The first release of Odin.

Odin (ᚨ) is a low-level emulator of the SEGA Hikaru arcade board. It runs the programs of the real chips wherever they are known, and draws with OpenGL or Vulkan. It is a hard fork of Valkyrie, by Stefano Teso.

## Games

All six Hikaru games, two of them in two versions:

- Air Trix (`airtrix`, `airtrixo`)
- Brave Firefighters (`braveff`)
- Planet Harriers (`pharrier`)
- NASCAR Arcade (`sgnascar`, `sgnascaro`)
- Star Wars Racer Arcade (`swracer`)
- Cyber Troopers Virtual-On Force (`von4`)

They play with a keyboard, mice, gamepads, wheels with force feedback (NASCAR) or light guns (Brave Firefighters). Each game is a MAME ROM and needs the BIOS `hikaru.zip` and `mie.zip` too.

## Downloads

| File | For |
|---|---|
| odin-v0.1.0-windows-x86_64.zip | Windows 10 or 11 |
| odin-x86_64.AppImage / odin-v0.1.0-linux-x86_64.tar.gz | Linux PC with glibc 2.38 or later (e.g. Ubuntu 24.04) |
| odin-aarch64.AppImage / odin-v0.1.0-linux-aarch64.tar.gz | Linux ARM64 with glibc 2.38 or later and OpenGL ES 3.1 |
| odin-macos.dmg | Mac with Apple silicon, macOS 13.3 or later |
| Odin-Artwork.zip | The title screens and bezels of the games |

## Xenra 0.5.0

### A new platform: iOS

Xenra ships on iPad and iPhone for the first time, as one app with both
consoles:

- Xbox 360 and original Xbox cores, the Metal renderer, JIT through StikDebug,
  and the floating pad with physical controller support.
- Dashboard, game library with box art and covers, setup wizard, per-game

  retail dashboard, all from the app.

The iOS and Android screens share their wording and layout, so a guide written
for one applies to the other.

### Original Xbox: the Performance core

The Performance core is the default original Xbox core on Android, chosen per
game at launch. xemu remains for the dashboard, the Insignia setup assistant and
the games the performance core cannot run, exactly the split the game menu
already understands. The core names in the library and per-game settings are now
Performance and Compatibility, matching the 360 side.

### Mali GPUs and compatibility rendering

## Back up before upgrading

Close the game and back up the complete save set (your saves folder), not only the GDD. Keep the GDD, its recovery and snapshot directories, and the `course-*` files together.
Tracks that use the new wind or CPU aggression settings save a newer settings block that 1.2.x cannot read. Tracks that do not use them stay readable by older builds. Keep your backup if you might go back to 1.2.x.

## New: G-Diffuser Companion (Windows and Linux)

The Windows x64, Linux x64 and Linux arm64 downloads now include the Companion, a separate desktop program in the `companion` folder inside your G-Diffuser folder. It builds the files G-Diffuser loads and checks every input before it builds. It never edits your settings, saves or stores.

releases.name: G-Diffuser 1.2.3 - Course Editor Hotfix
releases.body:
## Fixes
- Correct complete-course snapshot content binding so metadata-only edits do not reuse an incompatible retained snapshot.
- Handle terminal disk-write refusals without trapping Course Edit in its save wait loop.
- Fix the host editor's remaining 64-node admission ceiling. The supported total remains 127 nodes, including forks.
- Restore Content Library layout previews for supported tracks above 64 nodes.
- Adapt native load, overwrite, and delete confirmations to long filenames while keeping normal-size text and the Yes/No controls in place.
- Size the Course Edit information panel dynamically to fit the track title, length, and node count.

## Save compatibility — read before updating
Close the game and back up the complete installation save/state set before updating, not only the cartridge `.sav` file.

This release writes version-2 `.gcs` snapshots and still reads version 1. Older builds cannot read version-2 snapshots or packages that contain them. Before downgrading, restore the complete matching pre-upgrade save/state backup. Keeping old snapshots alone is not sufficient.

## G-Diffuser 1.2.2 - Save and Import Hotfix

- Fix disk-write ownership checks that could prevent Course Edit saves from completing and cause track imports to fail with MFS error 244.
- Preserve snapshot validation, rollback, and recovery protections during save and import operations.
- Add regression coverage using the production disk-write helper, including write failures and rollback.

Back up your installation's save and course-state files before updating. This hotfix does not change the course snapshot format.
